name: Hafsids of Béjaïa
alt: Hafsid branch of Bejaia and Constantine
Hafsid emirs of Béjaïa and Constantine

predecessors.name: Hafsid dynasty
predecessors.text: 'Abu Zakariya was recognised as ruler not only in Béjaïa but in Constantine, Algiers and Dellys'; Biskra, Ouargla and the Aurès are named as consolidated under him (no year)

successors.name: Spanish Bougie
successors.text: Béjaïa, taken by Pedro Navarro in 1510

successors.name: Kingdom of Beni Abbas
successors.text: the Kalaa in the Bibans, to which Emir Abderrahmane withdrew and where he 'set up a principality'

successors.name: Regency of Algiers
successors.text: Constantine, where the 1510 page has Abdelaziz's brother Abu Bakr as prince

ledger.x: 1285: Béjaïa and Constantine secede from the Hafsid domain of Ifriqiya.
Early 1318: the Hafsid domains are reunited.
1350 (bridge): Béjaïa is ceded to a cousin.
May 1366: Abu'l Abbas takes Béjaïa from Abu Abdullah.
1370: the western and eastern domains are reunited a third time.
Early 16th century (bridge, 1501): Béjaïa is independent of Tunis.
1510: Emir Abderrahmane withdraws to the Kalaa.

wars.name: Abu-l-Baqa's seizure of Tunis
wars.outcome: Abu-l-Baqa took Tunis in 1309 after seventeen days against the rival proclaimed there; a rebellion at Constantine led by his brother followed and he was assassinated; Abu Yahya Abu Bakr entered Tunis in early 1318 and reunited the Hafsid domains.

wars.name: Abu'l Abbas's reunification of Ifriqiya
wars.outcome: Abu'l Abbas took Béjaïa from Abu Abdullah in May 1366 and reunited the western and eastern domains, for the third time, in 1370.

wars.name: Spanish conquest of Béjaïa
wars.outcome: Pedro Navarro's expedition reached Béjaïa on 5 January 1510; the city fell in late May according to Arab sources; Sultan Abdelaziz's brother Abu Bakr, prince of Constantine, later killed him in battle at Takerkat (no year).

certainty.note: The page names towns and no frontier; whole provinces and 40-60 km circles are the researcher's.
